doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Childhood love of music and discovering record production
summary: Dorn grew up with his parents' classical and Broadway music and the wartime radio. He has no musical skills, so record production, like directing a film, suited him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was it, was there music in your household that got you —

Well there was always music. My father liked classical music, my mother liked popular music, you know, Broadway kind of music of the thirties, forties and fifties. And from as far back as I can remember I was in love with music. During World War II my uncle was stationed in New Guinea so my mother kept the — she had five cousins that were around the world — so my mother kept the radio on day and night to get war news you know. And when I was a year and a half old she used to play me Al Jolson records when I woke up. And there was a record called “April Showers” and I can remember back that far. It doesn’t sound like a person could but I can. And I would hear “April Showers” and I would cry. I was like hooked on music as far back as I can remember. And I have no skills. In other words I took music lessons for an hour and a half, you know I took a clarinet lesson. That didn’t work. And I can’t sing, I can’t dance, I can’t play an instrument, I don’t know how to do the technical side of making records. I can’t do © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

anything. But when I found out that there was something called record production where you were like the director of a movie but in terms of doing that to a record I said well okay, let me do this. You don’t have to have any talent you just have to have an instinct or something.
It’s something you’re born with, don’t you think?

I guess. I mean you know I would like to think I was born with an instinct to make records like other guys are born with, you know a great jump shot or the ability to hit a curve ball. If you want to glamorize it I’ll agree with you on that. I mean I don’t know. I mean I’ve kind of wandered aimlessly through life and developed a skill for wandering aimlessly through life, so I love to make records.
